persian_edits.before: **تعریف پیشنهادی نهایی ریشه:** «د م ر» در یکی از شاخه‌های کهن خود بر وارد شدن یا هجوم بردن به جایگاهی دلالت دارد، و در شاخهٔ مربوط به «دَمار» و «تَدْمِير»، بر هلاکت، نابودی و ویرانی شدید اطلاق می‌شود. در قرآن، تنها شاخهٔ نابودسازی حضور دارد و می‌تواند درباره انسان‌ها، جوامع و ساخته‌های آنان به کار رود. نوع، گستره و علت نابودی باید از مفعول، عامل و سیاق هر آیه شناخته شود؛ نه از خود ریشه به‌تنهایی.
persian_edits.after: **تعریف پیشنهادی نهایی ریشه:** «د م ر» در یکی از شاخه‌های کهن خود بر وارد شدن یا هجوم بردن به جایگاهی دلالت دارد، و در شاخهٔ مربوط به «دَمار» و «تَدْمِير»، بر هلاکت، نابودی و ویرانی شدید اطلاق می‌شود. در قرآن، تنها شاخهٔ نابودسازی حضور دارد و می‌تواند درباره انسان‌ها، جوامع و ساخته‌های آنان به کار رود. نوع، گستره و علت نابودی باید از مفعول، عامل و سیاق هر آیه شناخته شود؛ نه از خود ریشه به‌تنهایی. **معنای کوتاه ریشه:** هلاکت و نابودی شدید؛ تدمیر: نابود کردن یا ویران ساختن. در شاخهٔ دیگری از عربی، دَمَرَ به وارد شدن یا هجوم بردن گفته می‌شود.

Then We said: God’s command to Moses and Aaron.
Go, both of you: addressed to Moses and Aaron.
The people: the group who denied the signs.
They denied: rejected the divine signs as false.
Our signs: those that were denied.
The others: those outside the saved group in Lot’s narrative.
So look: a call to consider the outcome of the plotting.
Was: in asking how their plotting ended.
The outcome: the final result of their plotting.
Their plotting: the scheme whose outcome is described.
And their people, alongside the plotters in the account of destruction.
Altogether: comprehensiveness regarding the group in question.
The others, contrasted with the saved group in Lot’s narrative.
Travel through the earth: journeying to observe earlier peoples’ outcomes.
The earth: the setting of travel and observation of earlier peoples’ remains.
Then see: observing and considering predecessors’ outcomes.
Was: concerning the predecessors’ outcome.
The outcome: the fate of those who came before.
Before them: earlier peoples and groups.
And for the disbelievers: those concerned by the closing warning.
Similar outcomes: counterparts to the destruction just described.

Recursive paired survey found no authored reflection in the eight affected verses. All 69 paired lexical assignments match QAC. Preserve every nonempty context, unrelated metadata, grammar notices, canonical Allah, Arabic, translations, Fatihah, Baqarah through 160, shared code and earlier dirty/untracked work. Update only own summaries/preliminary notices and fill missing lexical contexts.

corrections: Installed complete reviewed Persian and full corresponding English: all 485 supplied logical blocks in each language, fourteen sections, 48 subheadings, eight morphology cards and 21 Arabic quotation blocks. Supplied Arabic quotations preserved apart from blockquote formatting markers and trailing whitespace. Brief root summary appended to final definition.

Confirmed ten occurrences in eight verses across eight surahs: eight Form II verbs and two Form II verbal nouns. Verified all 69 paired lexical root assignments in the edited units against QAC ROOT features; no reassignment needed. Distinguished seven perfect verbs from the wind’s imperfect tudammiru and preserved the cognate-accusative function without inventing a number of destructive episodes.

Checked Lisan’s exact damār and damara al-qawmu quotations and Ibn Faris’s entering-house and hedgehog quotations. Preserved both entering/incursion and destruction branches without asserting a proven historical derivation from one to the other. Distinguished Form I intransitive perishing from Form II transitive destruction.

Preserved Ibn Faris’s hunter-hide interpretation alongside the separately recorded fumigation explanation. Added the Aws collection’s alayha variant while retaining the supplied Maqayis alayhi Arabic. Qualified the pre-Islamic poet attribution so it does not by itself fix the particular witness’s composition date. Added a corresponding full sense translation in both languages, explaining Subah as a tribal name and saqaif as roofing slabs.

Confirmed Farazdaq attribution of the Thamud camel-foal witness, including Tabari’s editorial correction of an erroneous Jarir attribution elsewhere. Added full corresponding poetic translations identifying the satirical comparison’s contextual referent as Jarir. Kept the post-Quranic witness distinct from independent evidence of pre-Quranic usage or a historical account of Thamud’s destruction.

Preserved distinctions between destroying Pharaoh’s works, destroying groups of people, the wind as a natural agent, and dammara alayhim without inventing falling buildings. Retained context-limited kull shay and ajmain, with material remains neither denied nor assumed wholly intact. Kept moral blame separate from physical disaster and refused universal inferences about modern victims.

Corrected the Al-Naml salvation sequence: 27:52 describes remaining houses, while 27:53 identifies believers saved; it is not the immediately next verse after 27:51. Expanded 25:37–39 and 27:48–52 into individually named and verified references in both languages. Fourteen Quran quotations match installed Arabic after orthographic normalization: seven distinct full verses and seven distinct partial verses.

Preserved the source’s discussion of amarna, reported alternative readings, human responsibility and the distinction between command, disobedience and destruction. No installed verse reading, Arabic text, Persian translation or English translation changed. Root study notes do not replace independent reflection on divine justice or an event’s precise physical mechanism.

Required focused root-box check passed before installation for 138 complete lexical boxes.
